Paper Name: Components sizing of photovoltaic stand-alone system based on loss of power supply probability (Ayop et al., 2018)
NOTES: This paper is a PV/battery stand-alone system sizing study (no wind, no hydrogen, no fuel cell, no diesel generator, no electrolyzer). Many parameters are not applicable. The system uses PV arrays (5x5 configuration of Sunpower SPR-315E-WHT-D 315W modules) and East EA9010II lead-acid battery banks. The paper reports results for three methods: GCM (21 PV arrays, 57 battery banks), LCC (21 PV arrays, 57 battery banks), and RIM (22 PV arrays, 62 battery banks). Primary/baseline configuration used: LCC method (21 PV arrays, 57 battery banks). Rated power per PV array = 315W x 25 = 7875 W = 7.875 kW (paper says '7875 kW' but this is likely a typo for 7.875 kW or 7875 W). Total rated PV = 21 x 7.875 kW = 165.375 kW. Daily load = 813 kWh (paper also states 813,000 kWh in Table 5 but this contradicts the text '813 kW h' and annual 296,745 kWh; 813 x 365 = 296,745 confirms daily = 813 kWh). Annual load = 296,745 kWh. Battery: 48V, 10kW power rating, charging efficiency 80%, SOC operating range 20-80%. Inverter: Leonics Apollo STP-2110Cp, 4 units x 18 kW = 72 kW total, 415V, 50Hz. MPPT converter and inverter efficiency both set to 90%. PV panel life = 25 years, battery life = 7 years, power converter life = 13 years. Design/installation cost C0 = RM 150,000. PV module cost = RM 1,356 each, PV array cost = RM 33,900, battery bank cost = RM 4,868, total converter cost = RM 125,621. LCC at optimum (LCC method) = RM 1,512,771. Annual maintenance cost (LCC method) = RM 247,774. Initial cost = RM 1,264,997. Interest rate (I) and project life (n) are referenced in Eq.(14) but specific numeric values not explicitly stated in extracted text. LPSP target = 1%, actual achieved = 0.812% (LCC method) and 0.18% (RIM). LCOE not reported. No wind, hydrogen, fuel cell, electrolyzer, or diesel generator components in this system.
